title_en: Shanghai Zhongran Ship Fuel Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision — administrative penalty decision case
ruling_gist_en: Administrative normative documents, after being formulated, issued, published, and implemented, possess administrative legal effect as a basis for imposing administrative penalties. Whether to submit for record filing is not a prerequisite for the effectiveness of administrative normative documents; if an administrative normative document should have been filed but was not, this issue should be resolved through the statutory channels of internal supervision and inspection by administrative organs.
keywords_en: Administrative; Administrative Penalty; First Instance; Basic People's Court; Shanghai; Legal Person; State Organ; Shanghai Municipality Air Pollution Prevention and Control Regulations; Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China; Effectiveness of Administrative Normative Documents; Proportionality of Administrative Penalty; Relationship between Record Filing and Effectiveness of Normative Documents; Dismissal of Claims; Excessive Sulfur Content in Diesel Fuel; Application of Normative Documents; Combination of Punishment and Education
full_text_en:
Shanghai Zhongran Marine Fuel Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision — Dispute over Administrative Penalty Decision

Ruling Summary

An administrative normative document, once formulated, issued, published, and implemented, possesses administrative legal effect as a basis for imposing administrative penalties. Whether it has been filed for record is not a prerequisite for its effectiveness. If an administrative normative document should have been filed for record but was not, this issue shall be resolved through the statutory channels of internal supervision and inspection by the administrative authority.

According to relevant laws, regulations, and rules, if an administrative normative document in dispute differs to a certain extent from national standards, industry standards, local standards, and enterprise standards, and if it constitutes the basis for inspecting and determining the quality of ordinary diesel products produced and sold within a certain region, the implementation of such administrative normative document shall be considered in the review of the appropriateness of the administrative penalty. Therefore, the result of the penalty shall be adjusted by administrative discretion in accordance with the law to further enhance the appropriateness of the administrative penalty decision, so as to better reflect the principle of combining punishment with education in administrative penalties.

Plaintiff: Shanghai Zhongran Marine Fuel Co., Ltd., place of business: No. XXX, Sichuan North Road, Hongkou District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Sun Hougang, Chairman of the Company.

Defendant: Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision, place of business: No. XXX, Yishan Road, Xuhui District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Huang Xiaolu, Director of the Bureau.

Shanghai Zhongran Marine Fuel Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai Zhongran Company) initiated an administrative lawsuit with the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai against the Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai QTS Bureau) regarding a dispute over a quality and technical supervision administrative penalty decision.

The plaintiff, Shanghai Zhongran Company, alleged: The 0# ordinary diesel it sold was a qualified product conforming to GB252-2015 "Ordinary Diesel" (hereinafter referred to as the National Diesel Standard). According to the National Diesel Standard, the sulfur content requirement for ordinary diesel was upgraded from no more than 350 mg/kg to no more than 50 mg/kg, effective only from July 1, 2017. On March 24, 2016, the "Notice on Implementing the Same Sulfur Content Requirement for Ordinary Diesel as National IV Standard Vehicle Diesel" (Document No. 110 [2016] of the Shanghai Environmental Protection Bureau, hereinafter referred to as Document No. 110), jointly formulated by six departments including the Shanghai Environmental Protection Bureau, prematurely implemented the new standard for ordinary diesel. Document No. 110 was not filed with the Shanghai Municipal People's Government for record and thus was not a currently effective local product quality standard. The administrative penalty decision was based on provisions such as Article 47 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution," which conflicted with the provisions of superior laws such as the "Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution" and the "Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China." Therefore, the quality and technical supervision administrative penalty decision No. 2320170043 (hereinafter referred to as the Penalty Decision) issued by the defendant, Shanghai QTS Bureau, against the plaintiff on June 30, 2017, was unlawful. The plaintiff requested: 1. Revocation of the Penalty Decision; 2. Review of the legality of Document No. 110, which served as the basis for the Penalty Decision.

The defendant, Shanghai QTS Bureau, argued: Document No. 110, jointly issued by six departments including itself, aimed to comprehensively improve the quality of diesel used in non-road mobile machinery and inland vessels within Shanghai, reduce emissions from mobile sources of air pollution, and improve urban air quality. Document No. 110 was proactively disclosed to the public by the Shanghai Environmental Protection Bureau on March 25, 2016, and falls within the category of "quality standards prescribed by this Municipality" as referred to in Article 47, Paragraph 2 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution." It is a legal basis for determining the oil quality standards prescribed by Shanghai. The sulfur content of the 0# ordinary diesel in question exceeded the requirement set by Document No. 110, which prematurely applied the National Diesel Standard's provision of sulfur content no greater than 50 mg/kg to diesel used by non-road mobile machinery and inland vessels within Shanghai. Therefore, it could be determined that the plaintiff, Shanghai Zhongran Company, sold products that did not meet the quality standards prescribed by Shanghai. The Penalty Decision was reasonable and legally sound. As a leading enterprise in Shanghai's marine fuel supply and a subsidiary of a large state-owned enterprise, the plaintiff should have earnestly implemented relevant national and Shanghai environmental protection policies and taken the lead in strictly observing relevant laws and regulations. Accordingly, the defendant requested that the plaintiff's claims be dismissed.

Facts Found by the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai at First Instance:

On November 9, 2016, the defendant, Shanghai QTS Bureau, received a tip and conducted an on-site inspection at the plaintiff, Shanghai Zhongran Company's business premises located at No. 3500, Jungong Road, Yangpu District, Shanghai. The inspection revealed that storage tanks No. 5001 and No. 5003 contained 0# ordinary diesel in stock for sale. Shanghai QTS Bureau conducted the first sampling and testing of the 0# ordinary diesel from tanks No. 5001 and No. 5003. On November 14, 2016, Shanghai QTS Bureau was notified by the Shanghai Petrochemical Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Station that some indicators of the two samples from tanks No. 5001 and No. 5003 did not meet the relevant standards. Shanghai QTS Bureau then imposed administrative compulsory measures of sealing tanks No. 5001 and No. 5003 of Shanghai Zhongran Company and conducted a second sampling and testing of the oil products in both tanks. On November 15, 2016, Shanghai QTS Bureau received the first sampling inspection report from the Inspection Station, showing that the sulfur content of the 0# ordinary diesel in tank No. 5001 was 68.4 mg/kg, and in tank No. 5003 was 318.1 mg/kg. On November 21, 2016, Shanghai QTS Bureau received the second sampling inspection report from the Station, showing that the sulfur content of the relevant oil products in tank No. 5001 was 68.6 mg/kg, and in tank No. 5003 was 317.2 mg/kg. All four inspection reports issued by the Shanghai Petrochemical Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Station stated that the inspection basis was the technical indicators of the National Diesel Standard, and the determination basis was Document No. 110. Based on Document No. 110 jointly issued by six departments including the Shanghai Environmental Protection Bureau, Shanghai QTS Bureau determined that the sulfur content of the 0# ordinary diesel in tanks No. 5001 and No. 5003 exceeded 50 mg/kg, classifying them as non-conforming products. On November 16 and 21, 2016, respectively, Shanghai QTS Bureau informed Shanghai Zhongran Company of the test results of the two samplings, and on November 28, 2016, opened a case regarding the illegal act of selling non-conforming ordinary diesel by Shanghai Zhongran Company. Shanghai Zhongran Company did not apply for a retest.

After investigation and evidence collection, the defendant, Shanghai QTS Bureau, issued the Penalty Decision on June 30, 2017, finding that: The 0# ordinary diesel sold by the plaintiff, Shanghai Zhongran Company, was tested by the Shanghai Petrochemical Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Station, and its sulfur content exceeded 50 mg/kg, resulting in a determination of non-conforming product. It was found that from April 1, 2016, to November 2016, Shanghai Zhongran Company sold 687 tons of 0# ordinary diesel that did not meet the quality standards prescribed by Shanghai, with a value of RMB 3,281,000 (hereinafter the same), and illegal income of RMB 41,841.2. On May 22, 2017, the law enforcement officers served the administrative penalty notification letter to Shanghai Zhongran Company in accordance with the law. Shanghai Zhongran Company applied for a hearing, and Shanghai QTS Bureau convened an administrative penalty hearing in accordance with the law, issuing an opinion on June 26, 2017, agreeing with the proposed penalty decision. The main evidence included investigation transcripts, inspection reports, supply agreements, fuel supply records, sales invoices, rectification reports, and hearing transcripts. The actions of Shanghai Zhongran Company violated Article 47, Paragraph 2 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution." Pursuant to Article 93, Paragraph 1 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution" and Article 50 of the "Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China," the following administrative penalties were imposed: 1. Order to cease the sale of illegal products; 2. Fine of 0.5 times the value of the illegal products sold, totaling RMB 1,640,500; 3. Confiscation of illegal income of RMB 41,841.2; Total fines and confiscated amounts: RMB 1,682,341.2.

The Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai held at First Instance:

The defendant, Shanghai QTS Bureau, has the statutory administrative authority to investigate and penalize enterprises for selling non-conforming products in Shanghai. The sulfur content of the 0# ordinary diesel sold by the plaintiff, Shanghai Zhongran Company, in this Municipality was found to exceed 50 mg/kg in the four inspection reports issued by the Shanghai Petrochemical Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Station. Compared with the standard stipulated in Document No. 110, Shanghai QTS Bureau determined that the 0# ordinary diesel sold by Shanghai Zhongran Company did not meet the quality standards prescribed by this Municipality. The basis for issuing the Penalty Decision was sufficient, and the application of laws and regulations was correct.

Regarding the plaintiff Shanghai Zhongran Company's request for a legality review of Document No. 110: Document No. 110 was formulated to reduce emissions from mobile sources of air pollution and improve urban air quality, and it was proactively disclosed to the public by the relevant departments. It can serve as a legal basis for the defendant Shanghai QTS Bureau to determine the quality of oil products sold by Shanghai Zhongran Company. Therefore, the plaintiff's contention that the document is not a currently effective local product quality standard is untenable. Furthermore, the Penalty Decision targeted the sales conduct of Shanghai Zhongran Company. The scope of control of Document No. 110 covers the sales of oil used by non-road mobile machinery and inland vessels within the Shanghai area. Therefore, when Shanghai Zhongran Company sells ordinary diesel to inland vessels within Shanghai, it must comply with the relevant provisions of Document No. 110. In summary, the plaintiff's claims lack factual and legal basis and are not supported.

Accordingly, the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai, pursuant to Article 69 of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," rendered a judgment on February 22, 2018:

Judgment: Dismiss the lawsuit of Shanghai Zhongran Company.

Dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, Shanghai Zhongran Company appealed to the Shanghai No. 3 Intermediate People's Court, arguing: According to the National Diesel Standard, the sulfur content requirement for ordinary diesel was upgraded from no more than 350 mg/kg to no more than 50 mg/kg, effective from July 1, 2017. The 0# ordinary diesel sold by Shanghai Zhongran Company complied with the technical requirements of this national standard. Pursuant to Article 26, Paragraph 2 of the "Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China" and Article 27, Item (1) of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on Product Quality," it was a qualified product meeting national standards, and no situation existed where unqualified products were passed off as qualified. In issuing the Penalty Decision, the Shanghai QTS Bureau interpreted Document No. 110 as a local fuel quality standard authorized by Article 47, Paragraph 1 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution," and applied Article 27, Item (4) of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on Product Quality," which refers to "other provisions of laws and regulations." This lacks legal basis.

1. Article 47, Paragraph 1 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution" violates Article 9 of the "Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution" and Article 16 of the "Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China," and breaches Article 72 of the "Legislation Law of the People's Republic of China," which states that "the people's congresses and their standing committees of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, based on the specific conditions and actual needs of their respective administrative regions, formulate local regulations provided they do not conflict with the Constitution, laws, and administrative regulations." The formulation of Document No. 110 violates the principle of clarity in delegation. It not only fails to implement the normative source but also does not conform to the explicit delegated content and scope of Article 47 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution."
2. Document No. 110 violates Article 6 of the "Standardization Law of the People's Republic of China" (effective April 1, 1989), Articles 16 and 24 of the "Implementing Regulations of the Standardization Law of the People's Republic of China," and Article 14 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on Standardization," which require filing with relevant national administrative authorities for record before printing, publishing, and distribution. Therefore, it cannot constitute a currently effective local quality standard under delegated legislation.
3. Document No. 110, formulated on March 24, 2016, and implemented on April 1, 2016, violates Articles 8, Paragraph 3, 18, Paragraph 1, 24, and 30 of the "Provisions of Shanghai Municipality on the Formulation and Filing of Administrative Normative Documents" (Shanghai Municipal People's Government Order No. 26, effective May 1, 2010, hereinafter "Order No. 26"). Using Document No. 110 as the basis for the administrative penalty against Shanghai Zhongran Company does not comply with current laws and regulations. Furthermore, the Shanghai QTS Bureau failed to apply a mitigated penalty of less than 50% of the value as provided for in Article 55 of the "Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China."
   Request: Set aside the original judgment and instead grant the claims made in the original trial.

The Shanghai QTS Bureau argued:

1. Document No. 110 has a lawful basis for formulation. The "Shanghai Clean Air Action Plan (2013-2017)" formulated by the Shanghai Municipal People's Government on November 7, 2013, called for "prematurely implementing stricter oil product standards." On May 5, 2015, the National Development and Reform Commission and six other departments jointly issued the "Notice on Printing and Distributing the Work Plan for Accelerating the Quality Upgrade of Refined Oil Products" (Development and Reform Energy [2015] No. 974), clarifying that the 90th Executive Meeting of the State Council had approved the "Work Plan for Accelerating the Quality Upgrade of Refined Oil Products," which included among its main objectives "adding the content of upgrading ordinary diesel, and starting from January 1, 2016, supplying ordinary diesel with the same sulfur content as National IV standard vehicle diesel in key cities in the eastern region." To implement these requirements, the Shanghai Environmental Protection Bureau took the lead, and six departments jointly formulated Document No. 110 pursuant to Article 47, Paragraph 1 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution," prematurely implementing the relevant provisions of the National Diesel Standard.
2. According to Article 27 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on Product Quality," the basis for determining product quality standards includes not only national standards, industry standards, local standards, and enterprise standards but also "other provisions of laws and regulations." The limit on sulfur content for ordinary diesel set by Document No. 110 falls within the "local quality standard" stipulated in Article 47, Paragraph 1 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution."
3. Document No. 110 was formulated in accordance with the procedures stipulated by Order No. 26 and was published by the formulating authority on the official website of the Shanghai Environmental Protection Bureau on March 25, 2016. It is a valid normative document. Although it was not filed with the Shanghai Municipal People's Government for record after formulation, filing is not a necessary condition for the effectiveness of a normative document; it is a matter of internal assessment for administrative organs and does not affect its legal effect. Document No. 110 can serve as a basis for implementing administrative management and determining the quality of the products in question.
4. The Penalty Decision considered the specific circumstances of the case, including the facts, nature, and circumstances. Within the discretionary range of a fine of 50% to three times the value of the illegally sold products, the penalty was set at 50%. The findings of fact are clear, the evidence is conclusive, the application of law is correct, the procedure is lawful, and the discretion is reasonable.
   Request: Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

Facts Further Found by the Shanghai No. 3 Intermediate People's Court at Second Instance:

During the period from April to November 2016, the appellant, Shanghai Zhongran Company, sold 687 tons of the 0# ordinary diesel in question, detailed as follows: 113 tons in April with a value of RMB 477,850; 40 tons in May with a value of RMB 172,000; 72 tons in June with a value of RMB 324,000; and a total of 462 tons from July to November with a value of RMB 2,307,150, yielding an income of RMB 41,841.2. The total amount of fines and confiscated sums determined in the Penalty Decision was RMB 1,682,341.2, which has been paid. The other facts found in the original judgment are clear and are hereby confirmed.

Additionally, it was found that on March 24, 2016, the Shanghai Environmental Protection Bureau, the Shanghai Municipal Commission of Economy and Informatization, the appellee Shanghai QTS Bureau, the Shanghai Municipal Commission of Housing and Urban-Rural Development Management, the Shanghai Municipal Transportation Commission, and the Shanghai Municipal Agriculture Commission jointly formulated Document No. 110, which was published on the official website of the Shanghai Environmental Protection Bureau on March 25, 2016. The content of Document No. 110 is as follows:

"In order to implement the 'Shanghai Clean Air Action Plan (2013-2017),' ensure the realization of the upgrade requirements for ordinary diesel as set forth in the 'Notice on Printing and Distributing the Work Plan for Accelerating the Quality Upgrade of Refined Oil Products' (Development and Reform Energy [2015] No. 974) issued by the National Development and Reform Commission and six other departments, comprehensively improve the quality of diesel used by non-road mobile machinery and inland vessels in this Municipality, reduce emissions from mobile sources of air pollution, and improve urban air quality, the following matters are hereby notified: 1. From April 1, 2016, this Municipality will fully supply ordinary diesel with the same sulfur content as National IV standard vehicle diesel (i.e., sulfur content not exceeding 50 mg/kg). 2. From April 1, 2016, this Municipality will fully cease the supply, sale, and use of ordinary diesel that does not meet the above sulfur content requirement. 3. All producers and sellers of ordinary diesel shall organize their production and sales plans in accordance with this Notice. All sellers shall display the relevant contents of this Notice at their business premises and fulfill their obligation to inform relevant regulations to users and individuals."

The Shanghai No. 3 Intermediate People's Court held at Second Instance:

The appellee, Shanghai QTS Bureau, has the statutory authority to issue the Penalty Decision. The appellant, Shanghai Zhongran Company, raised no objection to the findings in the Penalty Decision regarding the quantity of the 0# ordinary diesel sold from April to November 2016, the value, the income amount, the conclusion that the sulfur content exceeded 50 mg/kg after testing, or the administrative enforcement procedure used to issue the Penalty Decision. These facts are confirmed. After synthesizing the arguments of both parties, the court summarizes the points of dispute and adjudicates as follows:

I. Regarding the appellant Shanghai Zhongran Company's challenge to the basis for formulating Document No. 110, i.e., Article 47, Paragraph 1 of the "Shanghai Municipal Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution," specifically, the dispute over whether Shanghai's relevant authorities could formulate local fuel quality standards stricter than the national standards.

Article 63, Paragraph 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that when hearing administrative cases, the people's courts shall take laws, administrative regulations, and local regulations as the basis. Local regulations apply to administrative cases occurring within the corresponding administrative region. The Regulations of Shanghai Municipality on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution, effective from October 1, 2014, constitute a valid legal basis applicable within the administrative region of Shanghai. According to Paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 47 of these Regulations, the municipal quality and technical supervision administration department may, based on actual circumstances and jointly with relevant departments, formulate local quality standards for vehicle, vessel, and non-road mobile machinery fuels that are stricter than the national standards. Fuels for vehicles, vessels, and non-road mobile machinery sold within this Municipality must comply with the quality standards prescribed by the State and this Municipality. Under the guiding principles of further strengthening air pollution control, improving ambient air quality, safeguarding the health of the people, and vigorously promoting ecological civilization construction, the *Shanghai Clean Air Action Plan (2013-2017)* and the *Work Plan for Accelerating the Upgrade of Refined Oil Quality*, approved at the 90th Executive Meeting of the State Council, explicitly set the target of "adding content for the upgrade of ordinary diesel. From January 1, 2016, commence supplying ordinary diesel with the same sulfur content as National IV standard vehicle diesel in key cities in the eastern region." Led by the Shanghai Municipal Environmental Protection Bureau, six departments jointly formulated Document No. 110 to implement the relevant provisions of the national diesel standard ahead of schedule. This has a sufficient policy and legal basis and is practically necessary and feasible. Therefore, the appellate opinion of Appellant Shanghai Zhongran Company that the fuel local quality standard provisions of Article 47 of the Regulations of Shanghai Municipality on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution conflict with superior laws is not adopted according to law.

II. Concerning Appellant Shanghai Zhongran Company's challenge to Document No. 110 as a local quality standard, i.e., the dispute over whether it constitutes "other provisions of laws and regulations."

The Regulations of Shanghai Municipality on Product Quality came into effect on September 1, 2012, and are also valid legal provisions applicable within the administrative region of Shanghai. Article 27 of the Regulations of Shanghai Municipality on Product Quality clearly stipulates that the bases for inspecting and determining product quality include: (1) national standards, industry standards, local standards, and enterprise standards; (2) contents expressly indicated on product labels or packaging, or quality status indicated by means such as product descriptions or physical samples; (3) technical specifications for product quality supervision and spot checks approved by the national or municipal quality and technical supervision departments; (4) other provisions of laws and regulations. Item (4) of this Article is designed to implement the requirements of other provisions of laws and regulations, ensuring comprehensiveness by establishing a catch-all clause. In the context of this case, Document No. 110, as the local fuel quality standard stipulated in Article 47 of the Regulations of Shanghai Municipality on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution, which is stricter than the national diesel standard, also constitutes a basis for inspecting and determining the quality of ordinary diesel products produced and sold in Shanghai. In other words, the local quality standard manifested as "other provisions of laws and regulations" is an independent basis for inspecting and determining product quality, distinct from the bases listed in items (1) to (3) of Article 27 of the Regulations of Shanghai Municipality on Product Quality, and is different from national standards, industry standards, local standards, and enterprise standards. Therefore, the appellate opinion of Appellant Shanghai Zhongran Company that Document No. 110 violates relevant standardization laws and regulations and cannot constitute a valid local quality standard under current authorized legislation is not adopted according to law.

III. Concerning Appellant Shanghai Zhongran Company's challenge to the validity of Document No. 110 as a basis for imposing administrative penalties, i.e., the dispute over whether it complies with the relevant provisions of Municipal Government Order No. 26.

Municipal Government Order No. 26 came into effect on May 1, 2010 (as amended, the Provisions of Shanghai Municipality on the Formulation and Filing of Administrative Regulatory Documents (Shanghai Municipal People's Government Order No. 46) came into effect on January 1, 2017). The purpose and basis of this regulation are to standardize the formulation and filing of administrative regulatory documents in Shanghai, strengthen the supervision and management of such documents, maintain legal uniformity, and promote law-based administration. Regarding its scope of application, it applies to the formulation, filing, and supervision and management of regulatory documents in Shanghai. Article 22 (Issuance) of Municipal Government Order No. 26 stipulates that regulatory documents shall generally be signed and issued by the principal responsible person of the formulating authority. The issuance of a regulatory document shall generally specify the formulating authority, document number, document name, date of issuance, and effective date. Article 23 (Promulgation), Paragraphs 1 and 2, stipulate that regulatory documents shall be promulgated to the public by the formulating authority; those not promulgated to the public shall not serve as a basis for implementing administrative management. Regulatory documents shall be published on the government website designated by the formulating authority and may also be published through newspapers, magazines, radio, television, and other news media. Article 24 (Effective Date) stipulates that the formulating authority shall specify the effective date of the regulatory document. A regulatory document shall take effect 30 days after its issuance, except in the cases listed in Article 21, Items (1), (2), and (3) of these Provisions, or where failure to take effect immediately after issuance would hinder the implementation of laws, regulations, rules, or national policies. Based on the above provisions, whether or not a document is submitted for filing is not a condition for the validity of a regulatory document. In the context of this case, Document No. 110, having been formulated, issued, promulgated, and implemented, possesses the administrative legal effect of serving as a basis for implementing administrative management. It should be noted that Article 44 (Supervision and Inspection), Paragraph 2 of Municipal Government Order No. 26 stipulates that the general offices (offices) and legal affairs offices of the municipal and district (county) people's governments shall supervise and inspect the formulation and filing of regulatory documents, urge the formulating authorities to promptly implement the relevant decisions of the municipal and district (county) people's governments and the legal suggestions of the legal affairs offices; and if they discover regulatory documents that should have been filed but were not, urge the formulating authorities to make up the filing within a specified period. After Document No. 110 was formulated, the lead formulating authority did not submit it to the Shanghai Municipal People's Government for filing pursuant to Municipal Government Order No. 26. This was indeed irregular in the work process and should be taken as a lesson. However, this does not constitute sufficient reason for Document No. 110 not to serve as a basis for implementing administrative management. This issue should be resolved through the statutory channels within the administrative organs for the supervision and inspection of the filing of regulatory documents. Therefore, the appellate opinion of Appellant Shanghai Zhongran Company that Document No. 110 violates the relevant provisions of the Provisions of Shanghai Municipality on the Formulation and Filing of Administrative Regulatory Documents and cannot serve as the basis for the administrative penalty imposed on Shanghai Zhongran Company is not adopted according to law.

IV. Concerning Appellant Shanghai Zhongran Company's challenge to the discretion exercised in the appealed penalty decision, i.e., the dispute over whether Article 55 of the Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China can be applied to grant a mitigated penalty of less than 50% of the value of the products sold to Shanghai Zhongran Company.

The 0# ordinary diesel sold by Appellant Shanghai Zhongran Company had a sulfur content greater than 50 mg/kg, failing to meet the requirements of Document No. 110, and was determined to be a non-conforming product. The facts are clear and the evidence is sufficient. Appellee Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision, when making the appealed penalty decision against Shanghai Zhongran Company, had already imposed the penalty at the statutory minimum rate of 50% of the value of the products sold. The application of the law was not improper. Looking back at the facts of the case, after Document No. 110 was published on the official website of the Shanghai Municipal Environmental Protection Bureau on March 25, 2016, and following investigation and inspection by the Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision, it was determined that Shanghai Zhongran Company continued to sell the involved 0# ordinary diesel for a cumulative period of 8 months from April 2016 to November 2016. Shanghai Zhongran Company's claim that it was unaware that the involved 0# ordinary diesel was a prohibited product and its opinion that the penalty should be below 50% of the value of the products sold are inconsistent with objective facts and common sense and are not adopted.

In conclusion, the illegal act of Appellant Shanghai Zhongran Company selling the involved 0# ordinary diesel in Shanghai that did not meet the requirements of Document No. 110 warrants a corresponding administrative penalty. However, considering the specific circumstances of this case, the facts have certain particularities. Since Document No. 110 stipulated the early implementation of stricter oil product standards, and from April 1, 2016, the comprehensive cessation of supply, sale, and use of ordinary diesel not meeting the sulfur content requirement of no greater than 50 mg/kg in Shanghai became inevitable, from a business operation perspective, the ordinary diesel previously stored and reserved in Shanghai by Shanghai Zhongran Company had to exit the Shanghai market, requiring a certain amount of time and cost for operational adjustment. Therefore, the base amount for the penalty can be adjusted according to law in terms of administrative discretion to further enhance the appropriateness of the appealed penalty decision, better reflecting the administrative penalty principle of combining punishment with education. Specifically, the administrative penalty of RMB 486,925 calculated by Appellee Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision for the 225 tons of products sold by Shanghai Zhongran Company from April to June 2016, with a total value of RMB 973,850, shall be deducted accordingly. Other aspects of the appealed penalty decision shall be upheld.

In light of this, the main content of the appealed penalty decision is modified *ex officio*, and the judgment of the court of first instance should also be reversed. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 77 and Article 89, Paragraph 1, Item (2) and Paragraph 3 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Shanghai No. 3 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on October 25, 2018:

1. The administrative judgment (2017) Hu 0104 Xing Chu No. 189 of Xuhui District People's Court, Shanghai, is reversed.

2. The main content of the Administrative Penalty Decision No. 2320170043 made by the Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision on June 30, 2017, is modified as follows: The original item 2, "2. Impose a fine of 0.5 times the value of the illegally sold products, amounting to RMB 1,640,500;" is changed to "2. Impose a fine of 0.5 times the value of the illegally sold products, amounting to RMB 1,153,575;". The original main content "Total confiscated illegal gains and fines amount to RMB 1,682,341.20." is changed to "Total confiscated illegal gains and fines amount to RMB 1,195,416.20."

3. The other claims of Shanghai Zhongran Marine Fuel Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

Court acceptance fees for the first instance and second instance are RMB 50 each, to be borne equally by Shanghai Zhongran Marine Fuel Co., Ltd. and the Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision, with each paying RMB 50.

This judgment is final.
